Project Zomboid is not just a game, it's hardcore survival simulator, It perfectly conveys the desperation, tension and thrill of surviving a zombie apocalypse. Every decision that you make matters, every mistake you make can be fatal to the story of your character. You can't win in this game, all you can do is postpone your imminent death. 
Gameplay wise the depths of mechanics is astonishing. It offers you fortifying a building or constructing your own base. The ability to pick traits and skill progression for your character adds a layer of strategy and the isometric graphics lend a retro charm to the grim setting. Multiplayer takes the experience onto a higher and different level, allowing you to build communities, roleplay, combat players. 
One of the most remarkable aspects of Project Zomboid is its thriving modding community, which has elevated the game to incredible heights. Mod makers deserve immense credit for their creativity and dedication, as they continuously expand and enhance the gameplay experience.

Project Zomboid is a message to survival enthusiasts, who want to deepen themselves in a post-apocalyptic world. The game will consume your life. Can't wait for Build 42.

Zomboid is probably the first real _survival_ game I've ever played. Forget survival horror, stupid stuff like that: this is the real deal. Yes, it's yet another zombie apocalipse game, but I think it's the first I've ever loved (I hate zombies since Doom... and Resident Evil made it no less boring for me).

The game attempts at mimicking reality goes a long way. Your character gets depressed, bored, sick; You have to avoid rain, can't carry a lot of weight... In fact, the only thing missing is having to use the bathroom, which, actually, is not really missed.

I strongly recomment this game. It's not a real sandbox - it's a game were you test your wisdom to see how long you can survive.

Great game for when you just hate yourself!

But seriously, if you feel like you should be able to do something in real life you can usually do it here using a similiar process. You think you should be able to create a wooden palisade? No problem!

Raid the police station for weapons? Sure! Bring a friend though!
Make a kickass stirfry? Add some hot sauce!
Survive the zombie apolypse? Yeah... Not bloody likely.

Make peace, you will die and it will be gruesome. Or you'll die of starvation huddled in a corner because you never left your house. Either way, you can have a lot of fun.

Disclaimer: I've only ever played multiplayer and I don't think it is worth it to play this on Single Player. Hearing your friends shouting over teamspeak that they're being eaten alive is the best part about this game.

At first, I was completely lost. I didn’t know how to defend myself, how to feed myself, or even how to stop the bleeding—and I died. Over and over.
But then I learned: you can clean dirty rags to prevent infections. You can repair your clothes with a needle and thread. Slowly, everything started to click.

The level of detail in *Project Zomboid* is incredible. Nearly every item has multiple uses, and survival is a constant learning experience.
Secure a safe place to sleep. Take advantage of electricity and water while they last. Barricade the doors and windows. Rest to regain your strength. Cut down trees, saw them into planks, and build a fortress.
Whatever your imagination can come up with, *Project Zomboid* probably lets you do it. Just don’t forget to watch your back.

And when you die—and you will—you can pick up where you left off. A new character, sure, but your predecessor would’ve wanted you to loot their corpse and raid their pantry.

On top of all that, the modding community has created an absolute treasure trove of content. From quality-of-life tweaks to complete overhauls, the sheer amount of customization is almost overwhelming—in the best way possible. Whatever experience you want, there’s probably a mod (or ten) for it.

Stay hydrated. Both in-game and in real life. It’s easy to lose track of time with this one.

This game is a blast to play, either solo or with friends. The graphics may look dated or just flat out ugly to some, but really try to look past this, as this game is going to be more dynamic and intense than any other survival game out there. Do you want a full medical system in play, where any small cut could become infected with the zombie virus, or just infected in general, and have to stay home instead of looting and gathering supplies while your body heals? Thats in the game. Do you want a game where you have to take care of your characters mental state? Oh yeah thats here. Pro tip, dont drink a full bottle of Ketchup. The game is so incredibly deep that you wont understand it all on your first run, or your first 10 runs. But you learn every time and get just a bit better.
